chapter_title: Concerning why Some shall delay to come forth from the Body, and Others die in an instant.
chapter_note: This kephalaion is extremely fragmentary. Most surviving material is dialogue/request frame (¶1, ¶3, ¶4). Only ¶2 preserves non-framing instructional content about differing death/release timings; despite low register scores (likely due to lacunae suppressing detectable vocabulary), its voice and subject matter fit the older explanatory teaching layer.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit dialogue frame and petition formula: “Once again… questioned… We beseech you, our master… instruct us…”. This is the Kephalaia hagiographic container, not the substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: The [sec]ond [ ... ] if he shall fall [ ... ... ] one [ ... ... ] one hour [ ... ... ] others who shall [ ... ... ] and they remain. They shall delay until they [ ... ... ] he is freed, and they delay to come toward [ ... ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: No dialogue attribution, no exhortation, no institutional application, no NT citation. It reads as impersonal mechanism about differential ‘delay’ in release from the body; heavy lacunae prevent seeing the full cosmological apparatus, so this core classification is somewhat tentative but best fits the remaining wording.
Second petition to the teacher (“we beseech you, our master…”)—a repeated Q&A frame element typical of the editorial compilation.
Dialogue attribution (“Then he says…”) without preserved teaching content; this is frame even though the substantive answer is lost in the lacunae.
